_about: Single source of truth for timing. animation.py (cameras, events, captions, titles) and tools/voiceover.py read this file. Times are seconds from the start of the video at 30 fps.

scenes.name: THE OPENING
scenes.desc: Darkness. A 1963 newspaper fades up under a single raking light; the camera pushes slowly toward the headline PRESIDENT KENNEDY ASSASSINATED.

shots.name: paper
shots.camera: Top-down push-in on the front page, 50 mm, shallow focus sliding onto the headline.

scenes.edit: Fade up from black over the first second; film grain throughout; low drone and a single piano note under the hook.

scenes.name: DALLAS, 1963
scenes.desc: Main Street, Dallas, at midday: period buildings and signs, crowds on the kerbs, broken cloud. The motorcade (police motorcycles, lead car, the dark-blue open presidential limousine, follow-up cars) moves west toward Dealey Plaza.

shots.name: main_high
shots.camera: High angle from an office window above Main Street, slow tilt-down as the motorcade approaches through the crowds.

shots.name: main_low
shots.camera: Low, respectful 3/4 view from the kerb, 85 mm, tracking with the limousine as it passes at a distance; flags fluttering.

scenes.edit: Dip to black into the street; crowd roar and motorcycle engines rise; cut between the two angles on a beat.

scenes.name: THE MOMENT THAT CHANGED HISTORY
scenes.desc: A wide, distant view of Dealey Plaza: the Texas School Book Depository, the Elm Street curve, the triple underpass. The motorcade turns onto Elm. Pigeons burst off the rooftops; the colour drains away. Nothing of the shooting is shown. A newspaper spins in: THE PRESIDENT IS DEAD.

shots.name: plaza
shots.camera: High wide view from above the south side of the plaza, very slow push; the motorcade small in frame.

shots.name: paper2
shots.camera: A newspaper spins up out of darkness toward the lens and settles on the investigators' desk.

scenes.edit: Hold the wide; at 'shots rang out' everything drops to near-silence and the picture drains of colour; pigeons scatter; a muffled drum roll leads into the spinning front page.

scenes.name: THE INVESTIGATION
scenes.desc: A 1960s police investigation room: blinds, haze, desk lamp, typewriter, newspapers, photographs, folders, a timeline board. A portrait-style card for Lee Harvey Oswald (no likeness: a silhouette and typed facts). A television flickers with a news bulletin.

shots.name: desk
shots.camera: Slow lateral dolly across the desk: newspapers, case folders, photographs, ending on the portrait card.

shots.name: card
shots.camera: Push-in on the portrait card and the typed statement, lamp light raking across the paper.

shots.name: tv
shots.camera: From behind the desk toward the TV set flickering in the dark corner, then drift to the board's timeline.

scenes.edit: Room tone, a ticking clock and distant phones; the TV crackles on at 'live television'.

scenes.name: THE QUESTIONS
scenes.desc: A dark archive: steel shelving, record boxes, light shafts through high windows. The Warren Commission and House Select Committee report covers. An acoustic-analysis printout. Declassified pages slide across the frame with 2025 and 2026 release stamps.

shots.name: archive
shots.camera: Dolly down the archive aisle toward a reading table; the Warren Commission report in a pool of light.

shots.name: reports
shots.camera: Over the table: the House Select Committee report slides in beside the Warren report; the acoustic printout.

shots.name: files
shots.camera: Top-down: declassified pages slide and stack across the frame, stamps landing.

scenes.edit: A slow, low pulse; paper slides and two stamp thumps on the release dates; a burst of radio static under 'acoustic evidence'.

scenes.name: THE FINAL SHOT
scenes.desc: Dealey Plaza at night, empty, in fog and lamplight. The camera pulls slowly backward and up. MORE THAN 60 YEARS LATER... then WHAT REALLY HAPPENED? Fade to black.

shots.name: night
shots.camera: Slow pull-back and rise over Elm Street toward the underpass, the Depository lit in the fog.

scenes.edit: Wind and a distant train horn; the final question lands on a deep low hit; fade to black over the last second.

lines.text: In under ten seconds, in Dallas, America lost a president.
lines.tts: In under ten seconds, in Dallas, America lost a president.

lines.text: November 22nd, 1963. President Kennedy came to Texas to mend a divided party.
lines.tts: November twenty-second, nineteen sixty-three. President Kennedy came to Texas to mend a divided party.

lines.text: At 12:30, in Dealey Plaza, shots rang out. Governor Connally was badly wounded. Thirty minutes later, the President was dead.
lines.tts: At twelve-thirty, in Dealey Plaza, shots rang out. Governor Connally was badly wounded. Thirty minutes later, the President was dead.

lines.text: That afternoon, police arrested Lee Harvey Oswald, who worked in the book depository above the route.
lines.tts: That afternoon, police arrested Lee Harvey Oswald, who worked in the book depository above the route.

lines.text: Charged with killing the President, he denied it. "I'm just a patsy," he told reporters.
lines.tts: Charged with killing the President, he denied it. "I'm just a patsy," he told reporters.

lines.text: Two days later, on live television, Jack Ruby shot and killed him. There would be no trial.
lines.tts: Two days later, on live television, Jack Ruby shot and killed him. There would be no trial.

lines.text: The Warren Commission said Oswald acted alone. In 1979, a House committee found a probable conspiracy,

lines.text: based on acoustic evidence scientists later disputed. Even files released as recently as 2026 have not ended the debate.

lines.text: More than sixty years later, one question still hangs over Dealey Plaza.
